answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost. A relic stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a crystal hold...
